title: Primitive-to-modern technology pathways: P1-P3 pilot
claim_ceiling: Conceptual graph only. No edge establishes a local process recipe, cost, timeline, safety, or physical reproducibility.

rules.requires_all: Every listed prerequisite must be qualified.
rules.requires_any: At least one listed alternative must be qualified; alternatives do not inherit one another's evidence.
rules.external_tokens: Tokens prefixed or named as imported, salvaged, qualified, or locally demonstrated are explicit scenario assertions and need their own evidence in any real profile.
rules.unknown_prerequisite: Unknown or conflicting prerequisites block the stronger capability claim; never assume true.
rules.evidence: Evidence attaches to a specific claim under a specific profile, not to a technology name globally.
rules.history: Edges are dependency hypotheses, not a universal chronology. Alternative modern routes may leapfrog historical stages but cannot erase their own real dependencies.
rules.physical_authority: No graph result grants authority to allocate resources, purchase, energize equipment, manufacture products, or operate machinery.

evidence_tiers.E1: Credible historical account or specialist reference.
evidence_tiers.E2: Directly documented process with known conditions.
evidence_tiers.E4: Field demonstrated under a bounded local profile.
evidence_tiers.E5: Reproduced by a separately operated node using transferred knowledge and qualified inputs.

sources.author: Lewis Dartnell
sources.title: The Knowledge: How to Rebuild Our World from Scratch
sources.use: Orientation and bibliography seed across agriculture, materials, power, transport, communications, chemistry and scientific knowledge.
sources.limits: Not a validated field manual; technical claims and conditions require specialist verification.

sources.title: Connecting the Scientific and Industrial Revolutions: The Role of Practical Mathematics
sources.use: Research anchor for relationships between practical mathematics, precision measurement, instrument-making and machine tools.
sources.limits: Historical explanatory evidence; not direct qualification of a modern local production route.

sources.title: The development and use of machine tools in historical perspective
sources.use: Research anchor for machine-tool development, productivity and industrial organization.
sources.limits: Historical overview; does not specify local input, cost or feasibility.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional craftsmanship
sources.use: Guidance on transmission and community context of traditional craft skills.
sources.limits: Not a technical process specification; community consent and knowledge restrictions must be respected.

sources.title: UNESCO: Transmission
sources.use: Guidance on knowledge and skills transfer across generations.
sources.limits: Not a technical process specification; practitioners remain active knowledge holders.

sources.title: RepRap Development Pathway
sources.use: Engineering analogy for replication factors and externally supplied non-printed components ('vitamins').
sources.limits: Project documentation, not a validated computer-manufacturing process or universal replication metric.

sources.title: Understanding Dependencies in the U.S. Semiconductor Supply Chain
sources.use: Motivates explicit multi-tier supplier and materials/equipment dependency records.
sources.limits: Sector-level supply-chain analysis, not local availability evidence.

sources.title: NIST CHIPS R&D Metrology Program
sources.use: Motivates explicit measurement, materials provenance, standards and test evidence in electronics manufacturing.
sources.limits: Program overview; does not qualify this pilot's processes or equipment.

sources.title: Nhyodyne: A Modular Backplane Computer
sources.use: Educational reference for modular computer boards, separate functions, Gerber availability and assembly from off-the-shelf components.
sources.limits: The repository README says the design is intended for hobbyist and educational use and discourages commercial use. Do not treat this as a commercial production base without rights/permission review. A Z80 system is not presumed capable of running a modern manufacturing workflow.

nodes.label: Observation, counting, shared measures and recordkeeping
questions: Which local measures are repeatable and comparable?
Who maintains records and teaches the practice?

nodes.label: Local resource, tool, energy and skill census
questions: Are inventories observed or only reported?
Which seasonal, ecological and access constraints apply?

nodes.label: Manual tools, workholding and basic repair
questions: Which tools and materials are actually present?
Which tasks require unrepresented specialist skill?

nodes.label: Bounded material shaping, joining and transformation routes
questions: Which resource and material grades are verified?
What energy, waste and ecological limits apply?
Which routes are locally demonstrated?

nodes.label: Repeatable measurement and reference-artifact continuity
questions: What is the uncertainty of the reference?
How is it checked and renewed?
Which claims require external calibration?

nodes.label: Renewable cutting tools, jigs, fixtures and workholding
questions: What material properties and tolerances are required?
Can wear surfaces and cutting edges be renewed?

nodes.label: A bounded useful-work drive or power input
questions: Is the resource seasonal?
Are bearings, lubrication, structures and guards available?
Can operating limits be established?

nodes.label: Use of an available machine tool for a bounded task
questions: Is the actual machine operational and correctly configured?
What tasks, materials and limits are qualified?
What does not follow about maintenance or local reproduction?

nodes.label: Production with a stated, valid inspection basis
questions: Are measurement uncertainty and calibration current?
Are material identity, process revision and acceptance criteria traceable?

nodes.label: Locally reproduced machine-tool capability
questions: Which spindles, slides, bearings, motors and controls remain external?
Can the calibration and cutting-tool renewal chains also be maintained?

nodes.label: Use of an existing or locally demonstrated electrical supply
questions: Are protection, insulation, grounding, storage and load limits qualified?
Which supply and replacement dependencies remain external?

nodes.label: Local reproduction of selected electromechanical equipment
questions: Which conductors, insulation, magnetic materials, bearings, controls and test equipment are mandatory?
What electrical safety and qualification evidence is required?

nodes.label: Use of an available computer or communications module
questions: What power, storage, interface, language and maintenance constraints apply?
What remains usable without the network?

nodes.label: Diagnostics and repair of selected electronic assemblies
questions: What test equipment, schematics and skills are available?
Which components can actually be replaced and tested?
What protections are required?

nodes.label: Advanced semiconductor-device manufacturing: placeholder with unresolved critical dependencies
questions: Do not count this node as closed until each required dependency is modeled and qualified.

nodes.label: Versioned, duplicateable technical knowledge packet and training path
questions: Are diagrams, worked examples, units, revisions, failure modes, rights and training/assessment methods included?
Can the packet be used offline?

nodes.label: Assemble a working computer from qualified modules and an exact BOM
questions: Is the exact BOM revision complete and all parts physically available?
Can a separate operator assemble and cold-boot it from the transfer packet?
Which modules remain imported and which are replaceable?

nodes.label: Fabricate selected computer enclosure, brackets, cooling ducts and fixtures locally
questions: Are the material, dimensions, thermal properties and mechanical loads qualified for this exact part?
What tooling, consumables and inspection evidence remain external?

nodes.label: Populate and test a board using purchased bare PCB and qualified electronic components
questions: Is the BOM and board revision frozen?
Can assembly quality and electrical behaviour be verified independently?
Which imported components are single points of failure?

nodes.label: Fabricate a bounded simple PCB locally under a qualified process
questions: Which board stack-up, conductor geometry, finish, insulation and test criteria are covered by this profile?
Are process wastes, safety, inspection and repeatability accounted for?

nodes.label: Build firmware and required software from versioned offline sources
not_implied: reproducibility of all upstream toolchain binaries unless separately tested
questions: Are source, dependency versions, build tools, firmware, licenses and recovery docs all preserved?
Does an independent rebuild match the declared reproducibility properties?

nodes.label: Host computer orchestrates a bounded, human-authorized cell that makes and tests computer subsystems
not_implied: local bare-PCB manufacture unless N20 closes
questions: Can the host create or select the revision-pinned artifacts, program the target, and produce a complete test receipt?
Which physical operations still require a human, vendor, or external service?

nodes.label: First copy is independently assembled, booted and qualified against the declared profile
not_implied: independence from imported ICs and tooling
questions: Did the copy cold boot and pass CPU/memory/storage/I-O tests after power removal?
Were every failed build, rework event and human intervention recorded?

nodes.label: The first clone independently operates the preserved workflow to build and qualify another copy
verification_protocol: power down or disconnect the original host from the active production workflow
start the documented workflow from the first clone
build, program, cold-boot and independently test a second copy
record every external service, human intervention, imported component and consumable
repeat with a separately operated node before making an E5 claim
questions: Does the copy possess the source, build tools, programming interfaces and process knowledge to repeat the workflow?
What exact imported items still bound the number of generations?
required_evidence: The original host is disconnected from the active production workflow.
The first clone runs the pinned manufacturing workflow using the preserved source/toolchain/design/firmware package.
The next copy is built, programmed, cold-booted and independently tested.
All imported parts, consumables, external services, human interventions and failed attempts are recorded.
The clone has not inherited a physical-closure claim merely because it can use imported devices.

profiles.notes: Profile claims are fixture inputs; presence of tools, materials and skills must be justified for any real place.
Possession does not prove operation, maintenance, repair, replacement-part production or reproduction.
Selected modern modules can be used without a local historical reconstruction sequence; upstream repair and supply dependencies remain visible.

required_future_tests: Use of imported equipment must not imply local manufacture of that equipment.
A machine's operation and the conformity of its output are separate claims.
Removing a required prerequisite must block closure unless a qualified alternate path is available.
Unknown critical semiconductor dependencies keep N15 blocked.
All proposed nodes remain E0 until claim-specific evidence is admitted.
The independent verifier rejects missing dependency tokens and forged transition receipts.

external_token_policy: Unknown or unsupported token stays unresolved. A token naming imported/salvaged/qualified equipment does not imply local maintenance, repair, replacement-part production, or reproductive closure.

computer_replication_benchmark.target: A modest, repairable computer/controller profile whose documented manufacturing cell can build a tested copy, then use the copy to build another copy under the same bounded profile.

levels.acceptance: Exact BOM, version-pinned documentation, cold boot, declared diagnostic suite.
Component-level repair and post-repair independent test; stock and imported replacement parts reported.
Specified enclosures, brackets, ducts and fixtures manufactured and inspected against declared criteria.
Assemble/rework and electrically test boards using bought bare PCBs and ICs; imported parts remain explicit.
Host runs the production workflow to build, program, cold-boot and qualify one copy.
Acceptance test: disconnect the original host, then have the first copy run the archived workflow to build, cold-boot and independently test the next copy.
A specific simple PCB route is locally demonstrated and inspected; no multilayer or silicon-fab inference.
Not achieved by the present pilot. Remains blocked until every critical semiconductor process dependency is modeled, sourced and independently qualified.

independent_metrics: BOM lines complete / unresolved; by count, sourced cost, mass where meaningful, and criticality—never one combined replication percentage
component classes still externally sourced and minimum-stock runway under declared production demand
conforming copies, failed builds, rework, scrap and operator interventions
energy, consumables, labor time, cycle time and equipment maintenance per accepted copy
number of complete reproduction generations demonstrated
capabilities and outputs that become blocked when each critical imported class is removed
independent evaluator agreement and separately operated-node reproduction
unrecorded manual interventions: target zero; any unrecorded intervention invalidates the claimed reproduction run
adversarial_tests: remove compute module or memory; system must not claim a complete computer was built
keep case and PCB but remove IC stock; no computer clone may be counted
invalid calibration or failed electrical acceptance test blocks qualification
source archive or required build toolchain missing; offline reproducibility claim is blocked
original host remains hidden in the C5 workflow; host-removal test must fail
missing failed-build records or unreported external service invalidates the result
change BOM revision between builds without requalification; result must show a revision mismatch
exhaust a critical imported IC stock; projections must show production blocked unless a qualified substitute route exists
successful board assembly cannot upgrade N15 semiconductor manufacturing closure
a second-generation copy that boots but cannot execute the manufacturing workflow does not pass C5
invariants: No single local/self-replication boolean or composite score.
Design, source generation, board assembly, bare-PCB fabrication, chip/package test and semiconductor die fabrication are distinct evidence-bearing claims.
Imported or salvaged hardware may satisfy use or assembly requirements but never automatically receives local repair/reproduction credit.
A simulation, netlist, PCB layout or firmware image is not evidence of a physically functioning computer.
No autonomous purchase, resource allocation or manufacturing actuation authority is implied.
computer_replication_benchmark.claim_ceiling: The current graph is E0 conceptual. C4/C5 remain proposed physical acceptance targets, not achieved results. This pilot does not imply local semiconductor die fabrication or indefinite industrial self-sufficiency.

candidate_platform_notes.proposed_use: C0-C3 research reference for modular boards, Gerber handoff, component procurement, assembly records and per-board replaceability.
candidate_platform_notes.not_a_claim: Not selected as the C4/C5 replication target; not presumed to run modern workcell tooling; not presumed available for commercial reuse.
required_review: capability fit for target test suite

candidate_platform_notes.proposed_use: Select a separate modest computer/controller profile that can run the archived production-control workflow needed to build and test another copy.
candidate_platform_notes.gate: Choose only after checking legal reuse, BOM completeness, runtime/toolchain fit, component availability, programming/debug interface, test fixture, energy needs and documented acceptance tests.
candidate_platform_notes.fallback: If no existing candidate passes, create a minimal original design from components/design artifacts with permission-cleared licenses and preserve a reproducible source history.
